questions.q: What is Server-Side Request Forgery in this lab?
o: Injecting SQL through a server-side template variable
Making the server fetch a URL that the attacker chose
Stealing cookies by forging a signed server response
Skipping input validation by sending extra HTTP headers
questions.x: The stock check posts a stockApi URL and the server fetches it. That request comes from the lab host, so it can reach internal HTTP services the browser cannot.
questions.h: The server is the HTTP client. Who chooses the destination URL it retrieves?

o: The internal host ignores HTTP and only speaks gRPC
The stockApi filter blocks that direct internal IP
The admin UI accepts HTTPS only, never plain HTTP
Port 8080 is dropped by the lab container firewall
questions.x: Direct internal addresses in stockApi are rejected as an invalid external stock check URL. The open-redirect chain works because the filter inspects the first URL, which is a same-site /product/nextProduct path.
questions.h: The error is about an invalid stock check URL. What class of destination is that filter trying to stop?

questions.q: Which endpoint is the open redirect, and which parameter holds the destination?
o: /admin/delete with a next= query pointing at any host
/product/nextProduct with a path= URL it redirects to
/product?productId= with a url= field in the HTML form
/stockApi with a redirect= header the browser follows
questions.x: GET /product/nextProduct?path= issues a 302 to whatever URL you put in path. The writeup shows path=http://portswigger.net as a 302 Location. That redirect is not SSRF by itself, because the endpoint does not fetch the target.
questions.h: The next-product link already contains a path query. Which path does the server copy into Location?

questions.q: How was the open redirect chained with the stock check SSRF?
o: stockApi was set to http://192.168.0.12:8080/admin directly
stockApi pointed at /product/nextProduct?path= the admin URL
A second browser tab requested the internal admin host directly
The Referer header was rewritten to the internal admin address
questions.x: stockApi was a same-site path: /product/nextProduct?currentProductId=1 and path=http://192.168.0.12:8080/admin. The filter allows the relative URL. The stock client then follows the 302 to the internal admin page.
questions.h: The filter sees the first hop. Which same-site endpoint can bounce that hop to 192.168.0.12:8080/admin?

questions.q: Why is the ampersand in the chained stockApi value sent as %26?
o: So the browser treats the admin URL as a fragment identifier
So path= stays inside stockApi instead of a second POST field
So the open redirect endpoint ignores currentProductId fully
So the URL filter sees a hostname and allows the internal IP
questions.x: The stock form is application/x-www-form-urlencoded. A raw & would start another body field, and path would never reach nextProduct. %26 keeps path= inside the stockApi value so the redirect target is the admin URL.
questions.h: stockApi is one form field. What happens to path= if you insert a literal & before it?

questions.q: Why does /product/nextProduct alone not give you SSRF?
o: It only issues a 302, it does not fetch the target server-side
It blocks every URL that does not start with /product?productId
It requires an admin session cookie the attacker cannot obtain
It rewrites path= to a relative path before sending the 302
questions.x: nextProduct returns 302 Location and stops. The browser would follow that redirect, not the lab server. SSRF needs the stock check, which performs an HTTP request and, in this lab, follows redirects.
questions.h: A 302 is not a server-side fetch. Which feature actually retrieves the Location URL from the lab host?

questions.q: Why does the stock check reach http://192.168.0.12:8080/admin after the 302?
o: The filter explicitly tells the HTTP client to follow redirects
The server-side HTTP client follows those redirects by default
The internal admin host forces a redirect on the first request
The lab proxies every 302 through an open internal mirror
questions.x: The stock feature is a server-side HTTP client. Clients like this follow 3xx responses unless told not to. After nextProduct returns 302, the same fetch continues to the internal admin URL the filter never saw.
questions.h: The filter checked only the first stockApi value. What default HTTP-client behavior continues the request after a 302?

questions.q: Which internal URL was the admin target used to delete carlos?
questions.x: The lab description gives the internal admin at http://192.168.0.12:8080/admin. A second chained stockApi uses path=http://192.168.0.12:8080/admin/delete?username=carlos to remove that user.
questions.h: The writeup uses a 192.168 address on port 8080. Which full admin URL is that?

questions.q: Which of these statements about this SSRF lab is correct?
o: stockApi blocks a direct internal IP
nextProduct path= is an open redirect
The stock client follows the 302
All of these statements are true
questions.x: Direct internal IPs in stockApi are filtered. /product/nextProduct?path= redirects to any URL. The stock-check HTTP client follows that 302, which is how the chain reaches 192.168.0.12:8080/admin.
questions.h: Filter, redirect, and follow-redirect are the three moving parts. Is any of those claims false in this writeup?

questions.q: Which of these statements about the exploit chain is correct?
o: nextProduct only issues a 302 Location
stockApi allows the internal admin IP
Only the browser follows the 302 chain
None of these statements are true
questions.x: The first statement is true. nextProduct only returns a 302, it does not fetch admin. stockApi still blocks a direct internal IP, and the stock-check server follows the 302. None is wrong because that 302 claim is true.
questions.h: Does nextProduct fetch the admin host, or only send a Location header?
